html:
SMTO-SKL-0078 — SMTO couldn't reach Microsoft 365 just now

GUID: d89909ed-f3dd-594c-b1cc-be632350e094
Slug: microsoft365-graph-transient
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • SMTO lost contact with Microsoft or ran out of time while reading, downloading or signing in. This usually clears on its own. If you were changing something, check whether it happened before trying again.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the computer running SMTO is connected to the internet and can open Outlook or OneDrive in a browser. SMTO needs a working connection to Microsoft to finish the request.
  2. Wait a minute, then ask SMTO again. For reading, searching or downloading, repeating is safe. Short outages at Microsoft or on the network usually clear quickly.
  3. If you were connecting your Microsoft account, ask SMTO to connect it again and use the new sign-in link. The old sign-in attempt didn't finish, and each link works only once.
  4. If you were uploading or changing something, check whether your action already happened in OneDrive or Outlook before asking again. Part of the change may already be done, and repeating it could duplicate it.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finishes the request, or your Microsoft account shows as connected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the time it happened, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't repeat a send, upload or other change until you've checked it didn't already happen.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Microsoft 365 call failed transiently: the 15-minute tool deadline passed, a read got a network error or 500/502/503/504 after its bounded retries, a download stream broke, or the OAuth token request during connect or refresh failed (network error or unexpected token-endpoint response).

What this means

  • Graph reaches a deadline, receives an eligible transient server failure, loses a transfer, or an OAuth transport AuthError is classified as transient. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Graph reaches a deadline, receives an eligible transient server failure, loses a transfer, or an OAuth transport AuthError is classified as transient.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect whether the failure came from authorization transport, deadline, provider status or transfer.

How to fix it

  • Confirm the Server host can reach graph.microsoft.com and login.microsoftonline.com and check Microsoft 365 service health, then repeat read operations. For a failed microsoft365.connect, start a new consent link; for an upload that stopped, inspect the destination before a new upload. Never replay a write with an unknown outcome.
  • Retry a bounded read after the provider becomes reachable. Never replay a write with an unknown outcome.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • A bounded read or supported auth flow completes after the actual condition clears; unknown writes are reconciled first.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
